proposals.expected_failure_mode: If the true admission lag is closer to 0 weeks or varies over the season, forecasts may show residual timing bias (early/late peak) and instability around the peak.
proposals.rationale: Primary anchor spec per feedback: SEIRS with fractional dynamics to flexibly capture sharp, high-amplitude peaks while mapping hospitalizations as a 1-week-lagged infection proxy to reduce phase error without over-lagging.

proposals.expected_failure_mode: If admissions systematically lag infections, removing delay can shift peaks earlier and degrade short-horizon forecasts during rapid rise/decline.
proposals.rationale: Small timing variant to test whether an explicit lag is necessary; keeps the same parsimonious SEIRS fractional backbone while removing delay to potentially improve peak alignment if admissions track infections more contemporaneously in this age group.

proposals.expected_failure_mode: May underperform if hospitalization dynamics behave like a lagged proxy rather than direct I; can produce phase errors and mis-scaled peak height when mapping is too direct.
proposals.rationale: Low-complexity comparator (no delay) to assess whether the delayed observation mapping is essential versus a direct infection-proxy observation; maintains fractional SEIRS to handle high peakiness with minimal structural change.
